title: Hand on heart - Pushing the , Investigation of the correlation between the stair climbing test and spiroergometric parameters in children of different age groups
summary:
The assessment of physical fitness and of the heart and lung function in children is of great importance not only for sport, but also in medicine. Climbing stairs is an everyday measure of physical performance that is often used as an indicator of a person's physical fitness.
An earlier study by our department has already shown that the values determined in the stair climbing test in healthy and overweight adults as well as children and adolescents with heart disease correspond well with the results from comparative examinations such as spiroergometry and the 6-minute walk test. This standardised protocol is now to be transferred to healthy children and adolescents who have taken part in the Hand on Heart project (DRKS 00033999).
At least 100 children of different ages will be examined as part of the project. The values measured during the stair climbing test will be systematically compared with the results of spiroergometry, an established gold standard in performance diagnostics. The stair climbing test is carried out a second time for the study in order to analyse the reliability of the test. This is followed by spiroergometry to validate the results.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents aged 10 to 18 who have already taken part in the "Hand on Heart" project
Exclusion criteria:
- Known cardiovascular diseases that lead to an unstable general condition (e.g. symptomatic cardiac arrhythmia, uncontrolled arterial hypertension, manifest heart failure)
- Metabolic diseases (e.g. hyperthyroidism, disorders of glucose metabolism)
- Diseases of the kidneys, liver or nervous system
- Mental illnesses
- Regular drug use, including nicotine and alcohol
- Regular use of medication (except hormonal contraceptives)
- Sudden cardiac death in the family history
